questions.title: The bony opening from the infratemporal fossa to the orbit
questions.question: Through which of the following bony openings is the infratemporal fossa directly connected to the orbit?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The superior orbital fissure connects the orbit to the middle cranial fossa, not to the infratemporal fossa.
explanations.B: Correct. The inferior orbital fissure lies between the greater wing of the sphenoid and the maxilla, at the junction of the floor and lateral wall of the orbit. It is the direct bony connection between the orbit and the infratemporal fossa, continuing posteriorly to the pterygopalatine fossa. It transmits the infraorbital and zygomatic nerves and vessels along this route.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The optic canal connects the orbit to the middle cranial fossa, carrying only the optic nerve and ophthalmic artery — a different route from the infratemporal connection asked about.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The pterygomaxillary fissure connects the pterygopalatine fossa to the infratemporal fossa, not the orbit directly to the infratemporal fossa.

questions.learning_objective: Name the inferior orbital fissure as the opening connecting the orbit to the infratemporal fossa.

questions.title: The infratemporal fossa's connection to the orbit, restated
questions.question: Through which of the following openings is the infratemporal fossa directly connected to the orbit?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The superior orbital fissure opens the orbit into the middle cranial fossa, a different destination from the infratemporal fossa.
explanations.B: Correct. The inferior orbital fissure sits between the greater wing of the sphenoid and the maxilla. It is the direct route between the orbit and the infratemporal fossa. It transmits the infraorbital and zygomatic neurovascular bundles along its length.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The optic canal carries only the optic nerve and ophthalmic artery into the middle cranial fossa, not into the infratemporal fossa.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The pterygomaxillary fissure connects the infratemporal fossa to the pterygopalatine fossa, not directly to the orbit.
